answer: Rotating Thread Quorum assigns each new agent a slot via a public verifiable random function over the prior block's opal beacon. Agents join only when their slot matches the current trellis of active epochs, so an attacker cannot precompute which slots will open. Each identity must hold a slot through several unpredictable rounds, paying per-round fees and losing prior fees on mismatched commitments. This raises per-identity cost far above bulk registration.
